Sir,
At 5.30p.m. 20-12-35, F.S. 22 Bruce came to the Station and
reported that anti-Kuomintang characters were found written in
Chinese ink on a wall inside the play ground of the Tsong Zah
(崇实) Commercial School at No. 906 Point Road.

"Down With Kuomintang and Facist (打倒國民黨法西斯)

REPORT

SHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
File No. REGISTRY
S. B. D. 6725
13 // 35
Date. November 18, 19 35

Subject Slogan writing in the International Settlement.

Made by and Forwarded by D. I. Ross

Since November 1, 1935, four instances of slogan
writing have come to the notice of the Municipal Police, two
in Chengtu Road district, one in Central and one in West
Hongkew (vide attached list). The slogans were of an anti-
Fascist, anti-Japanese and pro-communist nature, the first
named having been written in English and the other three in
Chinese.

The spreading of subversive propaganda by means of
slogan-writing on walls is usually manifest towards the
approach of communist anniversaries, national humiliation days
or on the occasions of important political happenings.
Offences of this nature are usually committed by junior members
of the Chinese Communist Party, the Chinese Communist Youth
League and their auxiliary organizations, whilst the slogans
which they are instructed to write, are previously formulated
by some responsible person of the propaganda section to which
they are attached. Chalk, Chinese ink and sometimes tar
are used for this purpose.

The combating of this kind of subversive activity has
proved a difficult task for the police in view of the fact
that the offence is invariably committed during the late hours
of the night and usually at places less conspicuous to police
patrols. Moreover, slogan writers are usually sent out in
parties of two or three so that while one does the writing,
the others keep a lookout for the approach of the police.

Offences of this nature could undoubtedly be lessened
to a considerable degree if police patrols, either in
uniform or plain clothes, were periodically instructed to be
on the lookout for, and challenge all suspicious persons

主题 公共租界内的标语书写事件。

由 D. I. Ross 制作并转呈

自1935年11月1日以来，工部局警务处注意到四起标语书写事件，其中两起在成都路区域，一起在中区，一起在西虹口（见附单）。这些标语具有反法西斯、反日和亲共性质，第一起是用英文书写的，其他三起是用中文书写的。

通过在墙壁上书写标语来传播颠覆性宣传的做法，通常在共产主义纪念日、国耻日或重大政治事件发生时表现得尤为明显。此类罪行通常由中国共产党、中国共产主义青年团及其辅助组织的初级成员实施，而他们受命书写的标语，则由其所属宣传部门的负责人预先拟定。为此目的使用的材料包括粉笔、墨汁，有时还有柏油。

鉴于此类罪行 invariably 在深夜犯下，且通常发生在警察巡逻不太显眼的地方，打击这种颠覆活动对警方来说已被证明是一项艰巨的任务。此外，标语书写者通常两三人一组出动，以便在一人书写时，其他人负责放哨，留意警察的接近。

如果定期指示身穿制服或便衣的巡逻警察留意并盘查所有可疑人员，尤其是那些在夜间游荡的学生模样的人，此类罪行无疑可以在很大程度上减少。在此方面，特别处可以通过派遣由中国侦探组成、在外籍警官监督下的小组，协助各巡捕房在可能发生标语书写的社区进行巡逻，特别是在“红色”纪念日之前及前夕。

我还建议通知各区主管和/或高级侦探，在转呈有关中文标语的报告时，除了罗马拼音版本外，还应附上中文字符。

（批：此提议正在关注中。JAG。）

File No. S. B. REGISTER

30

Subject Photographing Slogans on Walls and Posts.

Made by and Forwarded by D.S.I. Coyne.

I have to report having taken up the matter of
photographing slogans written on walls and posts with Supt.
Robertson, D.S. Mason and Clerk May Yoch.

Whilst D.S. Mason agrees that there would be no
difficulty attached to the technical side of the matter, Clerk
May Yoch is of the opinion that it would not be possible to
compare writing on a wall with a person's ordinary writing.

In addition to making allowance for difficulty in
writing on a perpendicular surface, the fact that the characters
would be drawn, and not written, must be considered. Even in
cases where the writing is in poster form, it is not likely
that the writing on two posters would be sufficiently similar
to justify the Police assuming that they were written by the
same person.

Under the circumstances it would appear that no
useful purpose would be gained by having photographs taken of
writings on walls or posts.

J Coyne
D. S. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).

（左侧批注：A1）
（左侧批注：S2, Please bring this matter to my notice again when fresh slogans are found. JM 15 AUG. 1935）

（底部手写批注：S2, Reference "A", the idea was to find out how many of the slogans were written by the same person, and the question of comparison with ordinary handwriting need not be considered. In reaching conclusions the height of the slogans from the ground & the colour of the paint used in making them, & other matters of handi-facino might be considered. JHS 15 AUG. 1935）

事由 拍摄墙壁及柱子上的标语。

撰写人及呈报人 副巡官科因 (Coyne)。

兹报告我已就拍摄墙壁及柱子上标语一事，与罗伯逊警司、梅森侦探警士及书记员姚克 (May Yoch) 进行了商讨。

虽然梅森侦探警士同意此事在技术层面并无困难，但书记员姚克认为，将墙上的字迹与个人的日常笔迹进行比较是不可行的。

除了需考虑到在垂直表面上书写的困难外，还必须考虑到这些字符是“画”出来的，而非“写”出来的这一事实。即使是在以海报形式书写的情况下，两张海报上的字迹也不太可能足够相似，从而使警方有理由假定它们是由同一人所写。

鉴于上述情况，拍摄墙壁或柱子上的字迹似乎达不到任何有益的目的。

J Coyne
副巡官。

政治部副主任。

（左侧批注：A1）
（左侧批注：S2, 请在发现新标语时再次提请我注意此事。JM 1935年8月15日）

（底部手写批注：S2, 参考“A”，其想法是为了查明有多少标语是由同一人所写，因此无需考虑与日常笔迹比较的问题。在得出结论时，可以考虑标语离地面的高度、制作标语所用油漆的颜色以及其他手工特征等事项。JHS 1935年8月15日）

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Report on Communistic Slogans found written on wall on Kiaochow Road near Changping Road.
At 9.25 a.m. 14/7/35, whilst on patrol on Kiaochow Road near Changping Road, C.P.C. 192 discovered the following Communistic Slogans written with black paint on the outside wall of the Gonzaga School on Kiaochow Road, near Changping Road.
C.D.C.16 made enquiries at the scene and took a copy of the slogans from the wall which read as follows:
(1) Strike to commemorate the May 30th.
（罷工紀念五卅）
(2) Down with the Imperialists.
（打倒帝國主義）。
The above slogans were immediately washed off by a station coolie.
Received at 11.35 am July 15.
T.G.
D.S.I.
Copy to Special Branch.
（批：holly 805 15/7/35）

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Report on Communistic Slogans written on walls on Changping Road and Hart Road on 25/5/35.
At 11 a.m. 25/5/35, C.P.C. 2670 reported to the station that the following Communistic slogans were found written with Chinese black ink on the walls on Changping Road and Hart Road.
C.D.S. 299 was detailed to make enquiries at the scene and took a copy of the slogans from the walls, translation of which are as follows:—
Changping Road
(1) Down with the Kuomintang Fascists.
(打倒國民黨法西斯)。
(2) Uphold and protect the Soviet.
(擁護蘇聯)。
(3) Join the Red Army (加入紅軍)。
(4) Down with the Imperialists.
(打倒帝國主義)。
(5) Strike to commemorate the May 30th.
(罷工紀念五卅)。
(6) Help the North-Eastern Volunteer Army.
(援助東北義勇軍)。
(7) Join the Communist Party
(加入共產黨)。
(8) Strike to commemorate the May 30th Anniversary
(罷工紀念五卅)。
Hart Road
(1) Join the Red Army.
(加入紅軍)。
(2) Uphold and protect the North-East Army.
(擁護東北軍)。
(3) The Soviet Government is the real government for freedom.
(蘇聯才是解放政府)
(4) Strike to commemorate the May 30th.
(罷工紀念五卅)。
(5) Down with Kuomintang
(打倒國民黨)。
(6) Join the Red Army.
(加入紅軍)。

Date May 16th 1935.

REPORT

Subject Report on Communistic slogans written on wall on Hart Road
near Changping Road and Singapore Road.

Made by D.S.I. Chu Meng Wei. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,
The undersigned begs to report that communistic slogans
(translated as follows) were found written on the walls on
Hart Road near Changping Road and Singapore Road at 5p.m. 16/5/35.
(1) Uphold and protect Soviet (擁護蘇聯 )
(2) Down with the Kuomintang betraying our country.
(打倒出賣中國的國民黨 )
(3) Oppose the 2nd time Great World War. (反對二次世界大戰 )
(4) Join the communist party. (加入共產黨 )
(5) Down with the Kuomintang. (打倒國民黨 )
(6) All Chinese should volunteer to oppose the Japanese
in the North of China. (中國人民自動北上抗日 )
The above slogans were erased by station coolie together
with C.D.C. 238 at 6.30p.m. 16/5/35.

Chu Meng Wei
D. S. I.

报告

主题 关于在哈特路（Hart Road）靠近昌平路和新加坡路（Singapore Road）的墙上书写共产主义标语的报告。

由 警探长 朱孟伟 制作。经由 [签名] 转呈

先生，
卑职谨此报告，于1935年5月16日下午5时，在靠近昌平路和新加坡路的哈特路墙上，发现写有共产主义标语（翻译如下）：
(1) 拥护苏联 (擁護蘇聯 )
(2) 打倒出卖中国的国民党。
(打倒出賣中國的國民黨 )
(3) 反对第二次世界大战。 (反對二次世界大戰 )
(4) 加入共产党。 (加入共產黨 )
(5) 打倒国民党。 (打倒國民黨 )
(6) 中国人民自动北上抗日。 (中國人民自動北上抗日 )
上述标语已于1935年5月16日下午6时30分，由巡捕房苦力会同便衣侦探 238 号擦除。

朱孟伟
警探长
